# Color, HDR, and fractional display references

`manifest.json` and the binary profiles in this directory are generated by
`scripts/generate-color-display-reference.py`. The generator has two modes:

```sh
python scripts/generate-color-display-reference.py
python scripts/generate-color-display-reference.py --check
```

`--check` is read-only. It hashes every saved profile, opens each profile with
LittleCMS, reruns the saved UInt16 transform, and checks the generated
MoonBit source. It does not call MoonAV1 and does not rewrite a file.
Profiles marked `Unsupported` are still independently decoded by LittleCMS
when an output exists; synthetic CMYK boundaries intentionally carry no RGB
output and are checked as rejection oracles.

The ICC oracle calls LittleCMS 2.19's public `cmsCreateTransform` and
`cmsDoTransform` ABI with native little-endian UInt16 pixels and
`cmsFLAGS_COPY_ALPHA`. The target is LittleCMS's own generated sRGB profile.
The 14-profile corpus covers matrix/TRC RGB v2 and v4, D65 and D50 gray TRC v2
and v4, Lab PCS v2/v4 encodings, `mft1` Lab, `mft2` Lab, v4 `mAB`, RGB
tetrahedral CLUT paths, and synthetic unsupported CMYK LUT boundaries. Ten
profiles are accepted by the public RGB/Gray API; Lab v2/v4 and CMYK v2/v4
are retained as four explicit rejection oracles.

The ICC policy is relative colorimetric with no black-point compensation:
`A2B1` is preferred and `A2B0` is used only when `A2B1` is absent. The
manifest retains LittleCMS's relative-colorimetric output (`intent=1`) and a
separate perceptual comparison (`intent=0`) for each transformable profile;
neither value is substituted for the other. Generated tests call the public
MoonBit API, allow at most 8 units per RGB channel, and require alpha to be
copied exactly. The BCHSW CLUT and CMYK boundary profiles are synthetic
LittleCMS outputs; all new profiles are synthetic/project-owned and no
installed HP, Agfa, SWOP or other printer profile is redistributed. The gray
profiles contain no external image data.

The 44 HDR cases use 100-digit Decimal arithmetic for actual 10/12-bit PQ
and HLG inputs, including mixed RGB values. PQ uses the absolute ST 2084
10000-nit scale; HLG uses the BT.2100 inverse scene-light curve and the
1000-nit display's system gamma of 1.2. The oracle independently applies
the luminance tone map and sRGB encoding, then emits integer RGBA16
expectations. Generated tests call the public API, allow at most one
UNORM16 unit per RGB channel, and require exact alpha.

The geometry vectors use exact Fraction arithmetic. They interpolate RGB after
premultiplying by alpha, interpolate alpha separately, divide only after the
interpolation, and round to UInt16 once in the input channel domain. Transparent
edges, half-pixel positions, a fractional origin, and a 2x2 bilinear grid are
included. These vectors are intended for the explicit fractional clap/resampling
API; integer display permutations remain covered by `avif_display_wbtest.mbt`.

The profile source and tool records are deliberately retained here rather than
depending on a host profile search during ordinary MoonBit tests. No photograph,
installed vendor profile or unpublished application output is included.
